glossary.definition: Call the model with tools, run the tools it requests, return the results, and repeat until it answers.
A cap on loop iterations or tool calls so an agent cannot run forever.
Depending on a framework’s abstractions so deeply that switching is costly.
In Pydantic AI, the typed model an agent’s final answer must validate against.
Passing resources such as a database client into an agent run instead of using globals.
LangGraph’s store that saves graph state after each step, per thread.
One saved conversation or case history that a run can pause and resume.
A LangGraph call that pauses a run for human input until it is resumed.
Transferring a conversation to another agent that then answers the user directly.
A guardrail result that stops an agent run immediately.
Code that runs at a point in the agent loop, such as before a tool call, and can block it.
In ADK, an agent that orchestrates sub-agents in sequence, in parallel or in a loop.
In CrewAI, a set of role-based agents working through tasks under a process.
Running long workflows so they survive crashes and resume from saved state.
A TypeScript schema library used to define and validate tool inputs.
AI SDK function that runs the tool loop and streams tokens and tool calls.
A LlamaIndex object that retrieves and synthesises an answer from an index.
A wrapper that lets an agent call a query engine as a tool.

sources.title: Atlan: Microsoft Agent Framework status (1.0 GA, April 2026)

symptomRouter.symptom: Our first agent, a few tools, small team
symptomRouter.advice: Write the loop yourself with a provider SDK; add a framework when a need appears.

symptomRouter.symptom: We want typed outputs and to switch providers easily
symptomRouter.advice: Pydantic AI: typed outputs and dependencies over most providers.

symptomRouter.symptom: Cases run for days and need human approvals
symptomRouter.advice: LangGraph with a Postgres checkpointer and interrupts.

symptomRouter.symptom: A triage agent should hand off to specialists, on OpenAI
symptomRouter.advice: OpenAI Agents SDK: handoffs, guardrails, sessions, traces.

symptomRouter.symptom: The agent must work with files, code and a shell
symptomRouter.advice: Claude Agent SDK, with narrow permissions and hooks.

symptomRouter.symptom: We are a Java or Go shop on Google Cloud
symptomRouter.advice: Google ADK: workflow agents in your language, A2A built in.

symptomRouter.symptom: The work splits into roles, or we are a .NET shop
symptomRouter.advice: CrewAI for Python role teams; Microsoft Agent Framework for .NET.

symptomRouter.symptom: The product team works in TypeScript and wants agents inside its web app
symptomRouter.advice: Use the Vercel AI SDK for typed tools and streaming, and Mastra for workflows that pause and resume.

symptomRouter.symptom: The agent mostly answers from large, messy document collections
symptomRouter.advice: Use LlamaIndex: parse and index the documents, give the agent a query engine tool, and save Context for long cases.
